{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1>THIS NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT ("Agreement"), made the ______ day of ____________, 1998, by and among [ ] (the "Selling Shareholder") and Dollar Tree Stores, Inc., a Virginia corporation ("Parent") and its wholly-owned subsidiary Dollar Tree West, Inc., a California corporation ("Sub") (Parent and its direct and indirect subsidiaries, including Sub, are referred to hereinafter as "Dollar Tree"). </SPAN 1><SPAN 2>W I T N E S S E T H:</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>WHEREAS, Selling Shareholder owns </SPAN 3><SPAN 4>_____________________ </SPAN 4><SPAN 5>percentage of all the issued and outstanding shares of stock of Step Ahead Investments, Inc., a California corporation ("SAI"); and</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>WHEREAS, concurrently herewith and pursuant to the Merger Agreement dated July 22, 1998, ("Merger Agreement"), Sub will be merged with and into SAI with SAI as the surviving corporation (the "Merger").</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>WHEREAS, concurrently herewith and pursuant to the Merger Agreement, all of the issued and outstanding stock of SAI will be converted into shares of common stock of Parent.</SPAN 7>
<SPAN 8>WHEREAS, Selling Shareholder acknowledges that </SPAN 8><SPAN 9>(i) SAI directly or indirectly operates stores, offices and distribution facilities under the name Step Ahead Investments and the tradenames "98CENTS Clearance Center" and "Clearance 98CENTS Centers" engaged in the retail and wholesale distribution of variety merchandise (the "Business"); </SPAN 9><SPAN 10>(ii) the Business is conducted in the United States; </SPAN 10><SPAN 11>(iii) the operation of the Business by SAI has given Selling Shareholder access to trade secrets of and confidential information relating to, the Business; and</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12>WHEREAS, the parties hereto agree that Selling Shareholder and Selling Shareholder's affiliates shall not compete (as described herein) with Dollar Tree for a certain period of time subsequent to the Effective Time as defined in the Merger Agreement in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth herein; and</SPAN 12>
<SPAN 13>WHEREAS, as a fundamental condition to the consummation of the Merger, the Selling Shareholder has agreed to enter into this Agreement, which is designed to ensure Dollar Tree receives the value of the Merger; and</SPAN 13>
<SPAN 14>WHEREAS, Selling Shareholder further acknowledges Dollar Tree may suffer irreparable damage should Selling Shareholder breach this Agreement.</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of good and valuable consideration described above and the covenants hereinafter set forth, the receipt and sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged by Selling Shareholder, and for the grant of [___________] options to purchase the stock of Parent pursuant to the terms of a separate option agreement, it is agreed as follows:</SPAN 15>
<SPAN 16>1. NON-COMPETITION COVENANT.</SPAN 16>
<SPAN 17>The Selling Shareholder acknowledges </SPAN 17><SPAN 18>(i) as an [director,] officer and principal shareholder of SAI, he has been instrumental in the Business of SAI and its success and </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>(ii) has been privy to and had access to the offices, personnel, technology, confidential and proprietary information of SAI.</SPAN 19>
<SPAN 20>1.1 Selling Shareholder agrees, during the period ending five years from the Effective Time ("Restricted Period"), neither Selling Shareholder nor any affiliate of Selling Shareholder shall conduct any of the following activities described in Sections 1.1.1, 1.1.2, and 1.1.3:</SPAN 20>
<SPAN 21>1.1.1 engage in Restricted Activities within the Restricted Area (as defined below); or</SPAN 21>
<SPAN 22>1.1.2 operate or promote within the Restricted Area a store using (or at least a 500 square foot area within a store dedicated to) a single price point retail concept selling goods at a single price point at or below $2.00; or</SPAN 22>
<SPAN 23>1.1.3 operate any variety, clearance, or close-out retail store in the same shopping center as any retail location of SAI existing as of the Effective Time or, in the case of an existing store of SAI not in a</SPAN 23>
<SPAN 24>shopping center, within one-quarter mile of such retail location. </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>1.2 Selling Shareholder agrees that, at no time after the Effective Time for so long as Dollar Tree or its successors carry on the Business, shall Selling Shareholder or Selling Shareholder's Affiliates operate any business </SPAN 25><SPAN 26>(a) under the names or names similar to "98 CENTS Clearance Center," "Clearance 98 CENTS Centers," "Everything 98 CENTS ... or less," or "Step Ahead Investments"; </SPAN 26><SPAN 27>(b) advertise or promote outside or within a store using the terms, or terms similar to "Everything 98 CENTS," 98 CENTS Clearance Centers," and "Clearance 98 CENTS Centers"; or </SPAN 27><SPAN 28>(c) under any name containing the words "98 CENTS," "Tree," or "Super Dollar," including their plurals. </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>1.3 </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>As used in this Agreement, the following terms have the following meanings:</SPAN 30>
<SPAN 31>1.3.1 a. While Selling Shareholder is a resident of California, "Restricted Area" shall mean all counties and cities in the States of California and Nevada in which SAI, as of the Effective Time, carries on the Business. </SPAN 31><SPAN 32>The covenant not to compete in the Restricted Area shall be construed as a series of separate covenants with regard to such city or county in the States of California and in Nevada.</SPAN 32>
<SPAN 33>b. If Selling Shareholder ceases to be a resident of California, immediately upon Selling Shareholder's change of residency "Restricted Area" shall mean each state in which either Dollar Tree or SAI, as of the Effective Time, has a store or otherwise carries on the Business. </SPAN 33><SPAN 34>The covenant not to compete in the Restricted Area shall be viewed as a series of separate covenants with regard to each state where either Dollar Tree or SAI carries on the Business.</SPAN 34>
<SPAN 35>1.3.2 "Restricted Activities" means the operation of </SPAN 35><SPAN 36>(i) a wholesale merchandise business that supplies stores of the type described in clause </SPAN 36><SPAN 37>(ii) hereof, or </SPAN 37><SPAN 38>(ii) any store engaged in the retail sale of goods (e.g., toys, health and beauty aids, food, books, party goods, stationery, hardware, housewares, jewelry, hair products, crafts, pet supplies, etc.) where at least eighty percent (80%) of such goods are sold at or below $2.00.</SPAN 38>
<SPAN 39>1.3.3 </SPAN 39><SPAN 40>A "shopping center" means a group of at least six (6) retail shops organized in a strip or mall configuration (but not necessarily in attached or adjacent buildings) sharing common parking areas and having the same landlord or leasing agent.</SPAN 40>
<SPAN 41>1.4 Selling Shareholder agrees that the restrictions in Section 1 are reasonable and necessary to protect the value of Dollar Tree, including the good will associated therewith, and do not unduly restrict Selling Shareholder's ability to earn a livelihood.</SPAN 41>
<SPAN 42>2. NO SOLICITATION AND NO HIRE OF EMPLOYEES. </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>Unless the parties hereto otherwise agree, Selling Shareholder agrees that from July 22, 1998 until the end of the Restricted Period, Selling Shareholder has not and shall not, directly or indirectly, hire or attempt to hire any employee of Dollar Tree or SAI, or solicit, induce, or attempt to solicit or induce (other than through newspaper classified advertisements) any employee of Dollar Tree or SAI to leave his or her job for any reason whatsoever without the written consent of Dollar Tree. </SPAN 43><SPAN 44>For purposes of this paragraph, an "employee" shall mean, as of any given date, anyone who has been an employee of Dollar Tree or SAI or any affiliate at any time during the four </SPAN 44><SPAN 45>(4) month period prior to such date.</SPAN 45>
<SPAN 46>3. RETURN OF PROPERTY. </SPAN 46><SPAN 47>All property, materials, memoranda, notes, lists, records and other documents or papers (and all copies thereof), including such items stored in computer memories, on microfiche or by any other means, made or compiled by or on behalf of SAI or its affiliates relating to or useful in the operation of the Business, are and shall be SAI's property ("Property") and all such Property that is confidential or that SAI does not have copies of shall be delivered to SAI at or prior to the Effective Time; provided, however, Selling Shareholder shall be allowed to retain copies of such Property necessary for Selling Shareholder to prepare, compute or support Selling Shareholder's tax returns or tax liabilities.</SPAN 47>
<SPAN 48>4. NON-DISCLOSURE OF CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION. </SPAN 48><SPAN 49>Selling Shareholder shall not, without the prior written approval of Dollar Tree, at any time copy, reproduce, disclose or divulge to any third party, use or permit others to use any confidential information of SAI or Dollar Tree (including financial information, sources of supplies and materials, prospective and existing expansion programs, joint ventures and affiliate agreements, business systems and marketing methods, and all business affairs). </SPAN 49><SPAN 50>During the Restricted Period, Selling Shareholder shall keep secret and retain in strictest confidence, and shall not use for the benefit of Selling Shareholder, Selling Shareholder's affiliate, or others, all confidential matters of the Business or of Dollar Tree, including trade secrets, details of supplier contracts, lease provisions and terms, operational methods and marketing plans or strategies. </SPAN 50><SPAN 51>Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing herein contained shall preclude Selling Shareholder from using the confidential information described in this Section 4 in the operation of or in the leasing of any real property or the operation of any business in connection with a business not coming within the definition of Restricted Activities or for other personal use, so long as such use does not conflict with any provision of this Agreement. </SPAN 51><SPAN 52>This Section 4 shall not apply if </SPAN 52><SPAN 53>(a) such information is already known to such party or to others not bound by a duty of confidentiality or such information is or becomes publicly available through no fault of Selling Shareholder or Selling Shareholder's Affiliates, </SPAN 53><SPAN 54>(b) the use of such information is necessary or appropriate in making any filing or obtaining any consent or approval required for the consummation of the closing under the Merger Agreement, or </SPAN 54><SPAN 55>(c) the furnishing or use of such information is required by legal proceedings.</SPAN 55>
<SPAN 56>5. COOPERATION. </SPAN 56><SPAN 57>Selling Shareholder agrees to cooperate in any reasonable manner with any reasonable requests by Dollar Tree from time to time to verify compliance with the provisions of this Agreement, provided, however, Dollar Tree shall reimburse Selling Shareholder for Selling Shareholder's reasonable out-of-pocket costs in complying with such request.</SPAN 57>
<SPAN 58>6. AFFILIATES.</SPAN 58>
<SPAN 59>6.1. Selling Shareholder agrees that the restrictions contained in Sections 1, 2, 3, and 4 above shall apply to any direct or indirect activities of Selling Shareholder whether conducted as </SPAN 59><SPAN 60>(i) an individual, </SPAN 60><SPAN 61>(ii) a partner (limited or otherwise) or joint venturer with any other person or entity, </SPAN 61><SPAN 62>(iii) an employee, agent or representative of any other person or entity, </SPAN 62><SPAN 63>(iv) as an officer, director or shareholder of any corporation (other than the ownership of less than 5% of the interests in a publicly traded entity), or </SPAN 63><SPAN 64>(v) as a member or manager of any limited liability company (other than the ownership of less than 5% of the interests in a publicly traded entity).</SPAN 64>
<SPAN 65>6.2. As used herein, the term "affiliate" with respect to any person shall mean any person or entity which controls such person, which that person controls, or which is under common control with that person. </SPAN 65><SPAN 66>In the case of Selling Shareholder, the term "affiliate" shall include the spouse, sibling, or lineal descendant or ancestor of Selling Shareholder, a trust for the benefit of any of the preceding, or any corporation, partnership, joint venture, or other entity which the Selling Shareholder, the spouse, sibling, or lineal descendant or ancestor of Selling Shareholder, or a trust for the benefit of any of the preceding, controls. </SPAN 66><SPAN 67>For purposes of the preceding sentences, the term "control" means the power, direct or indirect through one or more intermediaries, to direct or cause to the direction of the management and policies of a person or entity through voting securities, contract, or otherwise.</SPAN 67>
<SPAN 68>7. INJUNCTION; REMEDIES. </SPAN 68><SPAN 69>The Selling Shareholder acknowledges that Dollar Tree shall have no adequate remedy at law and that irreparable injury may result to Dollar Tree in the event Selling Shareholder violates or breaches any of the above agreements, covenants, or restrictions. </SPAN 69><SPAN 70>Therefore, it is hereby agreed that upon any breach of any of the above covenants, agreements, or restrictions, Dollar Tree shall be entitled, in addition to any other remedies available, to an injunction to restrain the violation or breach of any of the terms of such covenants, agreements, or restrictions by Selling Shareholder, and that no bond shall be required in procuring any such injunction. </SPAN 70><SPAN 71>In addition, if any party files suit to enforce its rights under this Agreement and prevails, the other party agrees to reimburse the prevailing party for all reasonable costs and fees, including any reasonable attorney's fees the prevailing party incurs. </SPAN 71><SPAN 72>The court shall determine who is the prevailing party for purposes of the preceding sentence. </SPAN 72><SPAN 73>The foregoing remedies for breach of this Agreement are cumulative and not exclusive of any other remedies Dollar Tree may have at law or in equity in the event of breach.</SPAN 73>
<SPAN 74>8. ENFORCEABILITY.</SPAN 74>
<SPAN 75>8.1 Selling Shareholder has examined this Agreement in detail, understands the nature of the burdens imposed by this Agreement, and is entering into this Agreement on Selling Shareholder's own volition. </SPAN 75><SPAN 76>Selling Shareholder has been encouraged by Dollar Tree to have this Agreement reviewed by Selling Shareholder's independent legal counsel and has had adequate opportunity to do so. </SPAN 76><SPAN 77>Selling Shareholder agrees that the restrictions, covenants and agreements contained in this Agreement are </SPAN 77><SPAN 78>(i) reasonable in all respects (including, without limitation, geographic area and duration), </SPAN 78><SPAN 79>(ii) necessary to protect the value of Dollar Tree, and </SPAN 79><SPAN 80>(iii) are not unduly harsh upon Selling Shareholder's ability to earn a livelihood. </SPAN 80><SPAN 81>Selling Shareholder represents that upon careful review, Selling Shareholder knows of no reason why any agreement, covenant, or restriction contained in this Agreement is not reasonable and enforceable.</SPAN 81>
<SPAN 82>8.2 </SPAN 82><SPAN 83>If any provision of this Agreement shall be found by any arbitration panel or court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or unenforceable, such provision shall be replaced by such panel or court by a valid and enforceable provision that will achieve, to the extent possible, the economic, business and other purposes of the invalid or unenforceable provision and, as modified, shall be enforced as any other provision hereof, all other provisions continuing in full force and effect to the maximum extent possible. </SPAN 83><SPAN 84>The enforceability of the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby.</SPAN 84>
<SPAN 85>9. NON-DISPARAGEMENT. </SPAN 85><SPAN 86>From and after the execution of this Agreement, the Selling Shareholder shall not make any material public statement, representation or communication of any sort, whether oral, in writing, or by any other medium, which disparages Dollar Tree, its directors, officers, shareholders, partners, employees, products, services or financial condition.</SPAN 86>
<SPAN 87>10. NO DEFENSE. </SPAN 87><SPAN 88>The existence of any claim or cause of action of the Selling Shareholder against Dollar Tree, whether predicated on this Agreement or not, shall not constitute a defense to the enforcement by Dollar Tree of the restrictions, covenants and agreements contained herein.</SPAN 88>
<SPAN 89>11. AMENDMENT AND MODIFICATION. </SPAN 89><SPAN 90>Subject to applicable law, this Agreement may be amended, modified and supplemented only by written agreement of Selling Shareholder and Dollar Tree at any time.</SPAN 90>
<SPAN 91>12. WAIVER OF COMPLIANCE; CONSENTS. </SPAN 91><SPAN 92>Any failure of the Selling Shareholder to comply with any obligation, covenant, agreement or condition herein may be waived only by a writing signed by Dollar Tree only and such waiver or failure to insist upon strict compliance with such obligation, covenant, agreement or condition shall not operate as a waiver of, or estoppel with respect to, any subsequent or other failure.</SPAN 92>
<SPAN 93>13. NOTICES. </SPAN 93><SPAN 94>All claims, notices, requests, demands and other communications required or permitted hereunder shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given or made </SPAN 94><SPAN 95>(i) upon receipt when delivered by hand or sent by overnight delivery by a nationally recognized private courier, </SPAN 95><SPAN 96>(ii) upon receipt for notices delivered by facsimile or </SPAN 96><SPAN 97>(iii) three (3) business days after being mailed, first class, certified mail, return receipt requested, with postage prepaid:</SPAN 97>

<SPAN 124>14. ASSIGNMENT. </SPAN 124><SPAN 125>This Agreement and all of the provisions hereof shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and any subsidiaries of Dollar Tree and their respective heirs, successors and permitted assigns, but neither this Agreement nor any of the rights, interests or obligations hereunder shall be assigned by any of the parties hereto without the prior written consent of the other parties.</SPAN 125>
<SPAN 126>15. GOVERNING LAW. </SPAN 126><SPAN 127>While Selling Shareholder is a resident of California, the Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of California, and the Courts of the State of California and the United States District Court for the Eastern District of California shall be the exclusive courts of jurisdiction and venue for any litigation, special proceeding or other proceeding as between the parties that may be brought, or arise out of, in connection with, or by reason of this Agreement. </SPAN 127><SPAN 128>If Selling Shareholder ceases to be a resident of California, immediately upon Selling Shareholder's change of residency, this Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the Commonwealth of Virginia, and the Circuit Court of the City of Norfolk and the United States District Court, Eastern District of Virginia, Norfolk Division, shall be the exclusive courts of jurisdiction and venue for any litigation, special proceeding or other proceeding as between the parties that may be brought, or arise out of, in connection with, or by reason of this Agreement. </SPAN 128><SPAN 129>The parties hereby consent to the jurisdiction of such courts.</SPAN 129>
<SPAN 130>16. COUNTERPARTS. </SPAN 130><SPAN 131>This Agreement may be executed in two (2) or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. </SPAN 131><SPAN 132>Dollar Tree and Selling Shareholder agree that at least two (2) completely executed counterparts of this Agreement shall be delivered to Dollar Tree and at least two (2) completely executed counterparts of this Agreement shall be delivered to Selling Shareholder.</SPAN 132>
<SPAN 133>17. HEADINGS. </SPAN 133><SPAN 134>The article and section headings contained in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not affect in any way the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement.</SPAN 134>
<SPAN 135>18. ENTIRE AGREEMENT. </SPAN 135><SPAN 136>This Agreement embodies the entire agreement and understanding of the parties hereto in respect of the subject matter contained herein. </SPAN 136><SPAN 137>There are no restrictions, promises, representations, warranties, covenants or undertakings other than those expressly set forth or referred to herein. </SPAN 137><SPAN 138>This Agreement supersedes all prior agreements and understandings between the parties.</SPAN 138>
<SPAN 139>19. CONSTRUCTION. </SPAN 139><SPAN 140>The parties hereto have participated jointly in the negotiation and drafting of this Agreement. </SPAN 140><SPAN 141>In the event an ambiguity or question of intent or interpretation arises, this Agreement shall be construed as if drafted jointly by the parties and no presumption or burden of proof shall arise favoring or disfavoring any party by virtue of the authorship of any of the provisions of this Agreement. </SPAN 141><SPAN 142>The word "including" shall mean including without limitation.</SPAN 142>
<SPAN 143>20. RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES. </SPAN 143><SPAN 144>Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as giving any person, firm, corporation, or other entity, other than the parties who are signatory hereto and their respective successors and permitted assigns, any right, remedy, or claim under or in respect of this Agreement or any provision hereof.</SPAN 144>
<SPAN 145>IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have made and entered into this Agreement under their hand and seal as of the date first hereinabove set forth.</SPAN 145>

guidance.when: Assessing whether return or destruction is required when the agreement or protected evaluation ends.
guidance.inspection: Identify both the required act and its trigger. Termination, expiration, conclusion of an evaluation, a determination that development cannot proceed, or cessation of interest qualifies when that event itself activates the duty. A request-only duty does not qualify. Nor does a party's unilateral decision not to proceed unless the clause treats that decision as the operative conclusion of the protected process.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete return-or-destruction duty together with its end-event trigger. Do not omit a governing introduction, and do not substitute a request trigger or a retention clause for the required end-event link.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exception to a return or destruction obligation.
guidance.inspection: Check whether the exception expressly permits continued possession of backups, archival material, a legal copy, or another defined subset after the return/destruction event. Conditions on access, purpose, or continuing confidentiality do not negate the permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention exception and, when separated, the governing return/destruction clause showing the temporal context.

guidance.when: The agreement requires return or destruction of confidential information and copies without stating a retention exception.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether the duty is exhaustive as to the covered material and copies. A complete return/destruction command that leaves no authorized retained subset negates permission to possess some material afterward.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the exhaustive operative duty and verify across the complete agreement that no backup, archival, legal-copy, or other retention exception qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses ownership, licenses, or rights in confidential information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Look for language that no license or right is granted, conveyed, conferred, or implied. A limited authorization to review or use information for the stated transaction does not by itself contradict the broader no-grant proposition.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the express no-grant clause; include an ownership clause only when it helps establish the object of the denied rights.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts disclosure of negotiations, discussions, a contemplated transaction, the agreement itself, or the existence of dealings.
guidance.inspection: A prohibition on revealing that negotiations or discussions exist establishes the hypothesis. A prohibition on public announcements concerning the agreement or transaction also qualifies; definition text alone must be paired with an operative nondisclosure duty.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative prohibition and the protected fact, retaining any governing introduction needed to connect a listed fact to the prohibition.

guidance.when: Confidential-information coverage is conditioned on marking, designation, or identification by the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the identification condition grammatically governs every covered disclosure mode. A single terminal condition may govern an enumeration of oral, written, and electronic modes; different procedures may also govern different modes. Do not treat nature- or circumstances-based coverage as identification.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete definition or all clauses needed to show that every disclosure mode is subject to identification by the disclosing party.

guidance.when: The definition covers information either expressly designated confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential from its nature or disclosure circumstances.
guidance.inspection: The contextual alternative independently covers undesignated information, so express identification by the disclosing party is not required for all confidential information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete alternative definition showing both designation and circumstance- or nature-based coverage.

guidance.when: Assessing whether the receiving party may make a copy in some circumstance.
guidance.inspection: Require an affirmative operational route for making copies, such as copies necessary for an authorized purpose or acknowledged backup creation. Prepared analyses or compilations do not by themselves authorize copying. A ban qualified by prior consent, and a remedy for unauthorized copying, are not affirmative permissions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the language that affirmatively authorizes, requires, or acknowledges copy creation and its condition; access, disclosure, derivative-document coverage, consent qualifiers, and breach-remedy clauses are insufficient.

guidance.when: The agreement prohibits copying confidential information and contains no affirmative operational copying route.
guidance.inspection: A direct copy ban, including a ban stated as applying without prior consent or approval, negates the benchmark permission hypothesis when the complete agreement does not otherwise authorize necessary copies, backups, or another copying circumstance. Do not convert the consent qualifier itself into affirmative permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the copy prohibition and verify across the agreement that no affirmative operational-copy or backup route qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure to representatives or other persons.
guidance.inspection: Resolve who falls within the permitted class. Consultants, agents, counsel, accountants, professional advisers, affiliates, and similar non-employees establish sharing with some third parties; an employee-only exception does not.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the permission and the definition or enumeration proving that at least one permitted recipient is a third party, plus any need-to-know or confidentiality condition governing the permission.

guidance.when: The agreement states an authorized transaction, project, evaluation, business relationship, or other defined purpose for confidential information.
guidance.inspection: A command to use confidential information only for that purpose, or not for any other purpose, directly imposes the limited-use obligation. The existence of the authorized purpose is not a contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use restriction and enough purpose language to identify the authorized scope.

guidance.when: Relevant candidate text is a numbered item, exception, continuation, anaphoric clause, or otherwise incomplete fragment.
guidance.inspection: Read the governing introduction and adjacent items to determine the item's legal function, trigger, subject, and exceptions. Keep independent operative clauses separately; do not treat a neighboring item as evidence merely because it shares the list.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every span necessary to make the relied-on proposition complete, while excluding sibling items that do not establish that proposition.

guidance.when: The confidential-information definition enumerates subject matter or data categories.
guidance.inspection: Find an expressly covered non-technical category, such as business, financial, marketing, personnel, customer, contact, or transaction information. Generic references to all information, documents, analyses, form, or derivatives do not alone prove non-technical coverage.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the definition and at least one explicit non-technical category; include continuation text when the category list crosses fragments.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exclusion, reservation, or acknowledgment concerning independent development.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that the receiving party may develop information independently without using or accessing the protected information. Prior approval to disclose, lawful receipt, or another unrelated exception does not establish independent development.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the independent-development clause with its governing exclusion or reservation language when needed to make its legal function complete.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses information obtained from an external source or later made available non-confidentially.
guidance.inspection: Require lawful receipt from a source other than the disclosing party or its representatives, with the source free of confidentiality restrictions, or a later non-confidential release that makes the information externally available. Independent development is different. Information supplied by a third-party vendor through the disclosing party is still disclosed through the protected channel and is not an acquisition permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the external-source or non-confidential-release item and its governing exclusion introduction, including the condition on the source's authority or confidentiality duty.

guidance.when: The definition or coverage clause addresses communication form.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether oral or verbal communication is expressly within confidential information, including language covering information irrespective of communication form or information disclosed in writing and also orally. Do not infer oral coverage merely from derivative notes or documents.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the language linking oral, verbal, or form-independent communication to confidential-information coverage, with any necessary definition continuation.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts recruiting, hiring, employment contact, or solicitation involving personnel of the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Find a prohibition on soliciting, employing, hiring, or initiating employment contact with officers, employees, or other personnel. Proxy solicitation, transaction standstill language, and general contact restrictions are not personnel nonsolicitation unless tied to employment or hiring.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative employment-related prohibition and the covered personnel class; include duration, targeting limits, or recruiting exceptions when they qualify the prohibition.

guidance.when: The agreement states that duties continue beyond an end event or remain effective for a post-event period.
guidance.inspection: Verify that confidentiality, non-use, or another agreement obligation continues after termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or an equivalent end of the protected relationship. Continuation merely after return or destruction does not establish survival of agreement termination.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the continuing obligation and the termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, or equivalent end event to which continuation is linked.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure or access to employees, internal staff, or a defined representative class.
guidance.inspection: Confirm an operative permission and that employees or internal staff belong to the permitted class. A definition naming employees is insufficient without a disclosure route; a permission to consultants, agents, or affiliates alone does not establish employee sharing.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the disclosure or access permission and, if the permission uses a defined class, the definition proving employees are included, plus material need-to-know or confidentiality conditions.

guidance.when: A clause permits or addresses disclosure compelled by law, regulation, court order, governmental demand, or legal process.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether that compelled-disclosure event requires notice, consultation, or equivalent advance communication to the disclosing party, subject to any legal-permission qualifier. A compelled-disclosure exception without a communication duty is insufficient, as is notice of an unauthorized disclosure after it occurs.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the compelled-disclosure trigger and the notice or consultation duty, including cross-referenced or list-introduction text needed to connect them.

guidance.when: The agreement affirmatively permits use of confidential information or defined residual information beyond a transaction-specific or otherwise stated agreement purpose.
guidance.inspection: A permission to use protected information for any purpose, or for the recipient's general internal business purposes without tying use to the agreement's stated purpose, negates an exclusive-purpose restriction. Merely allowing copying, disclosure, or conduct of a proposed relationship does not establish this contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the affirmative broad-use permission and any definition needed to show that it applies to confidential information or information retained from it.

guidance.when: The agreement states who may receive confidential information and the exception is limited to employees.
guidance.inspection: If disclosure is prohibited to everyone except qualifying employees, and the complete agreement supplies no permission for consultants, agents, advisers, or other non-employees, the agreement negates permission to share with third parties. A consent-based possibility alone is not an existing sharing permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the employee-only exception and the governing prohibition, and verify that no independent non-employee disclosure route qualifies it.
